data.narrative:
Hubble Network is a Series B-stage Space & Aerospace company that has raised $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 5 public tickers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Cowboy Space Corporation, Aalyria, and Skyryse, representing same-sector companies at Series B and Series C stages.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the $100M raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier typical of this stage transition, implies a valuation of $190M. Peer-median anchoring across four same-sector comparables—Sierra Space ($8.0B, Series C), Cowboy Space Corporation ($2.0B, Series B), Aalyria ($1.3B, Series B), and Skyryse ($1.1B, Series C)—yields a median of $1.6B with a range of $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple (27.4x median across the sector) cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $162M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $920M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in comparability: the peer set spans a 7x range at similar stages, suggesting either meaningful differences in technology maturity, market position, or growth trajectory among companies in the sector. Without revenue or unit economics, stage-based and peer-median methods provide bounds but limited precision on the most defensible point estimate.
